diagnosis: The incumbent is an over-jammed algebraic basin near cosine \(1/15\): at least 330 pairs are tied at the maximum to within \(10^{-16}\), every point has 21–40 contacts, and there are no rattlers. Its trust-region LP therefore has essentially no useful descent direction, while random kicks followed by smoothing or LP polishing either return to the same contact topology or worsen it; the \(7.4\times10^{-8}\) gain is only numerical squeezing of the same configuration. The missing structural property is a genuinely different, more heterogeneous topology—e.g. an asymmetric contact graph with some low-contact points, a different Gram spectrum, and unequal near-maximal pair levels that can be traded against one another. Several recent attempts also wasted the whole budget on expensive LP polishing of unpromising candidates, so topology search must be cheap, deadline-aware, and polish only after a candidate looks structurally new.
